claim: For the generalized matching count \(K_n^*=L_n+K_{n-L_n}\), with \(L_n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,\theta_n)\), the limits split into three regimes: if \(n\theta_n\to\lambda\), the count converges in total variation to \(\operatorname{Pois}(1+\lambda)\); if \(n(1-\theta_n)\to\mu\), the mismatch count converges in total variation to the Poissonized moved-point law with mass \(e^{-\mu}D_d/d!\sum_{j\ge0}\mu^{d+j}/((d+j)!j!)\); if both endpoint intensities diverge, the centered and scaled count converges to a standard normal law.

integrity: The universal limits are proved analytically; finite exact computations are consistency checks only.
The literature comparison is not exhaustive and no absolute priority claim is made.
limitations: No explicit convergence rate or finite-n total-variation bound is proved.
Endpoint limits assume the relevant intensity converges; oscillating sequences are covered only subsequentially.
The normal regime requires both n theta_n and n(1-theta_n) to diverge.
Related work on Poissonized permutation statistics may contain equivalent forms not found in the inspected sources.

title: A three-regime limit theorem for generalized matching counts
